newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- new issues fare well.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- new issues fare well.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds in late trade Tuesday held onto gains of 3/8 to up to 1/2 of a point. The rise was achieved on a rebound in Treasuries, and new municipal bonds met with fairly strong demand.
"I've got my high-grades up about an 0.02, maybe a little bit more, but not much. I've got my dollar bonds up 3/8 to a half, a tiny bit over 3/8," a municipal bond analyst said.
He added: "Activity was light to moderate and new-issue pricing was firm."
Goldman Sachs closed the account late Tuesday on a $140.5 million Mississippi general obligation bond deal, which the firm won at a 5.188 percent true interest cost.
While trading was subdued ahead of Friday's U.S. Independence Day holiday, a trader said that dealers might seek to take advantage of the quiet tone by trimming inventories.

The market was waiting for the conclusion of the Federal Reserve's two-day meeting of its policy making arm, which started on Tuesday. While no change in monetary policy was anticipated, that will not be enough to soothe all the market's concerns, as on Thursday, the vital payrolls data for June will be released. The report can spur a big reaction if it contains surprises.
There was speculation that cash-rich players, who have been waiting to see if bargains would emerge, might be forced to step up and buy if prices stay firm or keep rising.
"The market's got a good tone to it. It held its gains. I think that's forcing people to come in. There's a fair amount of money sitting on the sidelines," one trader said.

Wednesday's supply calender looked light, with only $32.2 million of competitive sales slated, while negotiated sales were expected to add up to $128.2 million, including $12 million of possible sales. The biggest negotiated sale was a nearly $75 million offering by Birmingham, Alabama.
In the secondary market, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, Airport Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5.4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.77 percent, NET, down five basis points.
And Detroit, Michigan, Sewer Disposal Revenues of 2022, which pay a five percent coupon, were offered at 5.55 percent, NET, unchanged.
September municipal bond futures ended up 19 ticks at 117-3/32, while the September Treasury bond futures climbed 20 ticks to 111-22/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 173 ticks.
